subject: the ten year is the truth
preheader: year-one cash flow lies. ten-year projection tells the truth.
headline: Year-one cash flow underrates good deals and overrates bad ones.
body: A new investor sees a property cash flowing $150/mo in year one and walks away. A pro looks at the same property and sees $1,400/mo in year ten. They're both right — about year one.

Why the gap? Rents grow about 3% a year over the long run. Expenses grow about 2.5%. The mortgage payment is fixed (if it's a fixed-rate loan). Principal pays down. Three slow tailwinds compounding for ten years turns a thin deal into a fat one.

Run the numbers. A $300,000 property renting at $2,400/mo with $2,250/mo total expenses cash flows $150/mo today. Project ten years with 3% rent growth, 2.5% expense growth, fixed PITI, and you're at roughly $1,300-1,500/mo cash flow by year ten. Plus you've paid down $40,000+ of principal. Plus appreciation.

The flip side is also true. A 'great' property with seller-financed assumable debt at 3.5% looks amazing in year one — but if the rent is already above market and the area is softening, year ten could be uglier than year one.

The 10-year projection is part of TrueCap Pro, alongside saved deals across devices and branded PDF exports — useful when you're presenting the long-run math to a partner, a lender, or yourself six months from now.
